recipes.title: Hellfoam: slip + acid + sleep, no lube (10 tiles)
recipes.tagline: Acid to wear them down, chloral to put them down; no fire; the foam itself does the slipping
recipes.what: Combat foam over up to 10 tiles (5u of trigger, tight foam). Floor-safe: nothing in it melts or burns away the floor tile. Slip: no lube. The foam itself is slippery for its 8 s life and nothing is left on the floor afterwards. Acid: 60u of fluorosulfuric acid, 192u per tile, 4.8u per tick. A person in a plain jumpsuit takes about 40.32 brute and 80.64 burn from it over the foam life (bare skin 161.28 / 322.56). It leaves an acid layer that eats items lying on the floor, but acid power 42 is far under the 200 that melts a tile. Sleep: 30u of chloral hydrate; a person in a jumpsuit absorbs 88u of it over the foam life (about 30u is enough for roughly 100 s of sleep after about 20 s of confusion and drowsiness).
recipes.notes: Needs a chem heater (400 K). The beaker stays hot for the later steps. Every chemical here is made from exact multiples of its ingredients, so nothing is left over in the foam. Fill: 100% of the beaker.
recipes.caution: Lethal-force chemistry: it burns, poisons and puts people to sleep. Law 1 and Law 2 apply: use it only on a clear threat (an antagonist already attacking the crew), never on someone you merely suspect. Fire and acid foam also reach YOU if you stand in it: trigger it at range and stay out.

recipes.title: Iron foam XL - 200 tiles (bluespace beaker)
recipes.tagline: Reinforced walls over a big area
recipes.what: Iron foam, exactly 200 tiles. About 8 seconds after it appears, every foam tile leaves a foamed-metal wall (reinforced, tougher than the aluminium walls).
recipes.notes: The metal goes in BEFORE the lithium so the reaction fires on the last click (lithium makes the foaming agent). One dispenser click is at most 100u, so putting the metal last would cap the reaction at about 165 tiles. 200 tiles is the exact fit: 40u of acid and 40u of foaming agent are all used up, so no acid ends up in the foam. A bigger 60u acid block would make 235 tiles but leaves 13u of acid in the foam. The last click is the 100u lithium button: the dispenser stops at the free space (40u), exactly what the 40u of hydrogen can turn into foaming agent. 60u of the metal is left over and harmless.
recipes.caution: Walls form on every foamed tile, including ones people stand on, so you can box people in. Never foam over injured crew or block medbay/escape routes. Bare hands bounce off the walls; any tool or weapon breaks them.
recipes.src: recipes/others.dm (metalfoam, ironfoam), effects_foam.dm (foamedmetal)

recipes.title: Neurine
recipes.what: Reacts with neural tissue, helping reform damaged connections. Can cure minor traumas.

recipes.title: Oculine
recipes.what: Quickly restores eye damage, cures nearsightedness, and has a chance to restore vision to the blind.
recipes.notes: The chem heater only approaches its target and never reaches it, so wait until its display shows the temperature in the step before you carry on. Reactions that need heat fire as soon as the beaker is hot enough.

recipes.title: Potassium Iodide
recipes.what: Heals low toxin damage while the patient is irradiated, and will halt the damaging effects of radiation. Can be used to decontaminate irradiated items.

recipes.title: Psicodine
recipes.what: Suppresses anxiety and other various forms of mental distress. Overdose causes hallucinations and minor toxin damage.

recipes.title: Spaceacillin
recipes.what: A generic antipathogenic agent.

recipes.title: Chloral Hydrate
recipes.what: A powerful sedative that induces confusion and drowsiness before putting its target to sleep.
recipes.caution: Knocks the target out, then poisons them. Law 1 applies.

recipes.title: Ephedrine
recipes.what: Increases resistance to batons and movement speed, giving you hand cramps. Overdose deals toxin damage and inhibits breathing.

recipes.title: Morphine
recipes.what: A painkiller that allows the patient to move at full speed even when injured. Causes drowsiness and eventually unconsciousness in high doses. Overdose will cause a variety of effects, ranging from minor to lethal.
recipes.notes: The chem heater only approaches its target and never reaches it, so wait until its display shows the temperature in the step before you carry on. Reactions that need heat fire as soon as the beaker is hot enough.
recipes.caution: Drowsiness and sleep at high doses.

recipes.title: Synaptizine
recipes.what: Increases resistance to stuns as well as reducing drowsiness and hallucinations.

recipes.title: Drying Agent
recipes.what: A desiccant. Can be used to dry things.

recipes.title: Firefighting Foam
recipes.what: A historical fire suppressant. Originally believed to simply displace oxygen to starve fires, it actually interferes with the combustion reaction itself. Vastly superior to the cheap water-based extinguishers found on NT vessels.

recipes.title: Formaldehyde
recipes.what: Formaldehyde, on its own, is a fairly weak toxin. It contains trace amounts of Histamine. When used in a dead body, will prevent organ decay.
recipes.notes: The chem heater only approaches its target and never reaches it, so wait until its display shows the temperature in the step before you carry on. Reactions that need heat fire as soon as the beaker is hot enough.
recipes.caution: A weak toxin in the living.

recipes.title: Hydrogen Peroxide
recipes.what: An ubiquitous chemical substance that is composed of hydrogen and oxygen and oxygen.

recipes.title: Space Cleaner
recipes.what: A compound used to clean things. Now with 50% more sodium hypochlorite! Can be used to clean wounds, but it's not really meant for that.

recipes.title: Space Lube
recipes.what: Lubricant is a substance introduced between two moving surfaces to reduce the friction and wear between them. giggity.
recipes.caution: Do not use on crew who must keep their footing.

recipes.title: Stabilizing Agent
recipes.what: Keeps unstable chemicals stable. This does not work on everything.

recipes.title: Sterilizine
recipes.what: Sterilizes wounds in preparation for surgery.
recipes.notes: The chem heater only approaches its target and never reaches it, so wait until its display shows the temperature in the step before you carry on. Reactions that need heat fire as soon as the beaker is hot enough.

recipes.title: Sulfonal
recipes.what: A stealthy poison that deals minor toxin damage and eventually puts the target to sleep.
recipes.caution: A poison. Law 1 applies.

recipes.title: Aiuri
recipes.what: Used to treat burns. Does minor eye damage.
recipes.caution: Costs minor eye damage for as long as it is in the blood.

recipes.title: Convermol
recipes.what: Restores oxygen deprivation while producing a lesser amount of toxic byproducts. Both scale with exposure to the drug and current amount of oxygen deprivation. Overdose causes toxic byproducts regardless of oxygen deprivation.
recipes.notes: The chem heater only approaches its target and never reaches it, so wait until its display shows the temperature in the step before you carry on. Reactions that need heat fire as soon as the beaker is hot enough.
recipes.caution: Makes a little toxin damage while it heals.

recipes.title: Cryoxadone
recipes.what: A chemical mixture with almost magical healing powers. Its main limitation is that the patient's body temperature must be under 270K for it to metabolise correctly.
recipes.caution: Only works while the patient is below 270 K (a cryo cell).

recipes.title: Granibitaluri
recipes.what: A mild painkiller useful as an additive alongside more potent medicines. Speeds up the healing of small wounds and burns, but is ineffective at treating severe injuries. Extremely large doses are toxic, and may eventually cause liver failure.

recipes.title: Helbital
recipes.tagline: brute, stronger the closer to death
recipes.what: Named after the norse goddess Hel, this medicine heals the patient's bruises the closer they are to death. Patients will find the medicine 'aids' their healing if not near death by causing asphyxiation.

recipes.title: Lenturi
recipes.what: Used to treat burns. Makes you move slower while it is in your system. Applies stomach damage when it leaves your system.
recipes.caution: Slows the patient while it is in the blood and hurts the stomach when it leaves.

recipes.title: Libital
recipes.what: A bruise reliever. Does minor liver damage.
recipes.caution: Costs minor liver damage for as long as it is in the blood.

recipes.title: Miner's Salve
recipes.what: A powerful painkiller. Restores bruising and burns in addition to making the patient believe they are fully healed. Also great for treating severe burn wounds in a pinch.
recipes.caution: Hides pain, so a patient may not notice how hurt they are.

recipes.title: Oxandrolone
recipes.what: stimulates the healing of severe burns. Extremely rapidly heals severe burns and slowly heals minor ones. Overdose will worsen existing burns.

recipes.title: Probital
recipes.what: Originally developed as a prototype-gym supliment for those looking for quick workout turnover, this oral medication quickly repairs broken muscle tissue but causes lactic acid buildup, tiring the patient. Overdosing can cause extreme drowsiness. An Influx of nutrients promotes the muscle repair even further.

recipes.title: Salbutamol
recipes.what: Rapidly restores oxygen deprivation as well as preventing more of it to an extent.

recipes.title: Salicylic Acid
recipes.what: stimulates the healing of severe bruises. Extremely rapidly heals severe bruising and slowly heals minor ones. Overdose will worsen existing bruising.

recipes.title: Saline-Glucose Solution
recipes.tagline: brute, burn and a blood substitute
recipes.what: Has a 33% chance per metabolism cycle to heal brute and burn damage. Can be used as a temporary blood substitute, as well as slowly speeding blood regeneration.

recipes.title: Tirimol
recipes.what: An oxygen deprivation medication that causes fatigue. Prolonged exposure causes the patient to fall asleep once the medicine metabolizes.
recipes.caution: Puts the patient to sleep once it has metabolised.

recipes.title: Atropine
recipes.tagline: rapidly stabilises a patient in crit
recipes.what: If a patient is in critical condition, rapidly heals all damage types as well as regulating oxygen in the body. Excellent for stabilizing wounded patients, and said to neutralize blood-activated internal explosives found amongst clandestine black op agents.

recipes.title: Epinephrine
recipes.tagline: slowly heals a patient in crit
recipes.what: Very minor boost to stun resistance. Slowly heals damage if a patient is in critical condition, as well as regulating oxygen loss. Overdose causes weakness and toxin damage.

recipes.title: Ammoniated Mercury
recipes.what: Quickly purges the body of toxic chemicals. Heals toxin damage when in a good condition someone has  		no brute and fire damage. When hurt with brute or fire damage, it can deal a great amount of toxin damage.  When there are no toxins present, it starts slowly purging itself.
recipes.notes: The chem heater only approaches its target and never reaches it, so wait until its display shows the temperature in the step before you carry on. Reactions that need heat fire as soon as the beaker is hot enough.

recipes.title: Antihol
recipes.what: Purges alcoholic substance from the patient's body and eliminates its side effects.
recipes.notes: The chem heater only approaches its target and never reaches it, so wait until its display shows the temperature in the step before you carry on. Reactions that need heat fire as soon as the beaker is hot enough.

recipes.title: Calomel
recipes.what: Quickly purges the body of all chemicals except itself. The more health a person has,  the more toxin damage it will deal. It can heal toxin damage when people have low enough health.
recipes.notes: The chem heater only approaches its target and never reaches it, so wait until its display shows the temperature in the step before you carry on. Reactions that need heat fire as soon as the beaker is hot enough.
recipes.caution: Hurts healthy people with toxin damage.

recipes.title: Diphenhydramine
recipes.what: Rapidly purges the body of Histamine and reduces jitteriness. Slight chance of causing drowsiness.

recipes.title: Haloperidol
recipes.what: Increases depletion rates for most stimulating/hallucinogenic drugs. Reduces druggy effects and jitteriness. Severe stamina regeneration penalty, causes drowsiness. Small chance of brain damage.
recipes.caution: Slows stamina regeneration.

recipes.title: Higadrite
recipes.what: A medication utilized to treat ailing livers.

recipes.title: Inacusiate
recipes.what: Rapidly repairs damage to the patient's ears to cure deafness, assuming the source of said deafness isn't from genetic mutations, chronic deafness, or a total defecit of ears.
recipes.notes: The chem heater only approaches its target and never reaches it, so wait until its display shows the temperature in the step before you carry on. Reactions that need heat fire as soon as the beaker is hot enough.

recipes.title: Mannitol
recipes.what: Efficiently restores brain damage.

recipes.title: Multiver
recipes.what: A chem-purger that becomes more effective the more unique medicines present. Slightly heals toxicity but causes lung damage (mitigatable by unique medicines).
recipes.notes: The chem heater only approaches its target and never reaches it, so wait until its display shows the temperature in the step before you carry on. Reactions that need heat fire as soon as the beaker is hot enough.
recipes.caution: Can hurt the lungs unless the patient has several other medicines.
